scope: Offline CPU-evaluated production Registry/Studio/Animator/EquipmentPose and actual NPC/Player flows, rendered with Blender. No replacement controller or synthetic skeleton. Browser gameplay, WebGL/Electron rendering and GPU performance are unverified.

before: Cloth uses fitted helper bones and baked poses; no dynamic cloth collision.
Hard angular inner-sleeve folds remain visible in some raised-arm poses; localized lining closes the reviewed openings without claiming smooth cloth simulation.
The existing two-handed axe support hand retains its partly open/sliding source pose, emphasized by the low-poly fingers.
The target-only grounded death retains a slightly propped prone shape from the authored motion; contacting extremities do not imply a fully flat torso.
Raw source-mode bow poses may hover: gameplay retains the bow pelvis while replacing leg tracks with locomotion legs, and the fitted contact bake preserves that composed stance.

Per-frame locomotion planting removes authored airborne run clearance. Actual idle/run fades on the reviewed fitted targets can briefly dip soles about 2.5–4.7 cm; source-clearance-preserving locomotion remains unfinished.
The inherited short early two-handed-axe runtime transition can briefly dip feet about 2–4 cm; the shared blend and body/root behavior are unchanged.
Coarse LOD2 final death contact can retain about 3.7–7.5 mm of surface-floor penetration under the shared identical animation.
LOD2 retains a small dark angular hood fold and coarse hard edges; the large posterior inner-shell crossings were repaired with paired lining.

The widest steel sword grip retains a broad low-poly C silhouette around its raised rings in extreme closeups; the corrected grasp preserves blade orientation with a bounded local attachment translation.

Corrected right-hand skin changes authored non-sword fingertips. Coarse one-handed axe haft overlap remains and can be deeper than the original; this repair does not claim zero weapon/hand penetration.

knownVisualLimitations: Nordic steel sword retains a coarse C-shaped hand silhouette and visible gap at extreme close range.
Nordic foot T5 has 3 sampled hand vertices inside the actual handle, maximum nearest-surface depth 2.091mm; mounted approval is not a perfect-contact claim.

Nordic 1H axe grip overlap exists in b211 and increases from 25.918 to 32.505 mm on foot (.28/.55), and 28.005 to 31.255 mm mounted (.28). 2H sampled maximum decreases 27.214 to 25.315 mm. Actual closed-mesh ray parity; vertex sampling is not a global triangle penetration bound.
Coarse LOD hand simplification and angular authored non-sword finger contours remain.
Previously documented cape/elbow/hood, early transition floor and propped death limitations remain; historical b211 sheets are not relabeled as current hand-rig images.
